title: An anti-FAP-scFv-functionalized exosome-carrying hydrogel delivers SKI mRNA to fibrotic nucleus pulposus cells to alleviate intervertebral disc degeneration by regulating FOXO3.
authors: Li, Yueyang; Zhai, Yu; Wang, Tianling; Wang, Siya; Tian, Yu; Bian, Zhiqun; Zhang, Yang; Zhang, Chao; Liu, Minghan; Li, Changqing
one_liner_zh: 该文研究外泌体水凝胶递送SKI mRNA缓解椎间盘退变，核心是纤维化治疗与TGF-β信号通路，无蛋白质-DNA互作、结合位点预测或AI/物理模拟建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Rationale: Nucleus pulposus (NP) fibrosis is a contributing factor to intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD), which lacks an effective treatment. This study focuses on elucidating the role and mechanisms of the TGF-beta signaling repressor SKI in NP fibrosis and exploring its therapeutic potential. Methods: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) was used to investigate fibrotic nucleus pulposus cell (NPC) subsets and assess TGF-beta signaling activation. Two recombinant plasmids encoding single-chain variable fragments (scFvs) targeting the fibrotic NPC marker FAP and SKI mRNA were co-transfected into HEK-293T cells to yield functionalized exosomes (EX(ski+scFv)). The addition of EX(ski+scFv) to a gelatin/oxidized sodium alginate hydrogel produced a pH-responsive exosome/hydrogel system named Gel@EX(ski+scFv). The therapeutic effects and underlying mechanism of Gel@EX(ski+scFv) were evaluated by RNA sequencing, molecular docking and coimmunoprecipitation. Results: A fibrotic NPC subset was characterized by elevated FAP and diminished SKI expression, along with activation of the TGF-beta signaling pathway. SKI overexpression reduced fibrosis in TGF-beta-treated NPCs. EX(ski+scFv) successfully delivered SKI mRNA to FAP-expressing fibrotic NPCs. Gel@EX(ski+scFv) possessed good mechanical properties, degradability, injectability, and biocompatibility. Gel@EX(ski+scFv) effectively alleviated NP fibrosis and IVDD in rats. RNA sequencing, molecular docking and coimmunoprecipitation revealed that SKI could interact with FOXO3 to suppress the TGF-beta signaling pathway. Conclusion: This study elucidates the mechanism by which SKI-mediated TGF-beta signaling inhibition alleviates NP fibrosis. The development of the Gel@EX(ski+scFv) system for the targeted delivery of SKI mRNA offers a promising therapeutic strategy to alleviate NP fibrosis and IVDD in the future.
abstract_zh: 理由：髓核（NP）纤维化是椎间盘退变（IVDD）的一个促成因素，目前缺乏有效治疗方法。本研究旨在阐明TGF-β信号抑制因子SKI在NP纤维化中的作用及机制，并探索其治疗潜力。方法：采用单细胞RNA测序（scRNA-seq）研究纤维化髓核细胞（NPC）亚群，并评估TGF-β信号激活情况。将编码靶向纤维化NPC标志物FAP和SKI mRNA的两个重组质粒共转染至HEK-293T细胞，产生功能化外泌体（EX(ski+scFv)）。将EX(ski+scFv)添加到明胶/氧化海藻酸钠水凝胶中，构建了pH响应性外泌体/水凝胶系统，命名为Gel@EX(ski+scFv)。通过RNA测序、分子对接和免疫共沉淀评估Gel@EX(ski+scFv)的治疗效果及潜在机制。结果：纤维化NPC亚群的特征是FAP表达升高、SKI表达降低，并伴随TGF-β信号通路激活。SKI过表达减少了TGF-β处理的NPC中的纤维化。EX(ski+scFv)成功将SKI mRNA递送至表达FAP的纤维化NPC中。Gel@EX(ski+scFv)具有良好的机械性能、可降解性、可注射性和生物相容性。Gel@EX(ski+scFv)有效缓解了大鼠的NP纤维化和IVDD。RNA测序、分子对接和免疫共沉淀揭示，SKI可与FOXO3相互作用以抑制TGF-β信号通路。结论：本研究阐明了SKI介导的TGF-β信号抑制缓解NP纤维化的机制。开发用于靶向递送SKI mRNA的Gel@EX(ski+scFv)系统，为未来缓解NP纤维化和IVDD提供了一种有前景的治疗策略。
